name: Increasing the weight of a fault gadget
summary: For fault boundedness, the weight of a fault gadget may be increased, or a fault-free gadget made noisy.
description:
A fault gadget with weight $w$ is *fault-bounded* by the same gadget with weight $w'$ if $w \geq w'$ or $w = -$ (the edge is fault-free on the left-hand side). Fault boundedness is the one-directional version of fault equivalence: $D_1$ is fault-bounded by $D_2$ if every undetectable fault on $D_1$ has a fault of at most the same weight with the same effect on $D_2$. So this is a directed rewrite, not a fault-equivalence. Added to the complete rules for fault equivalence it gives a complete calculus for fault boundedness, and together with [the w-fault equivalence rule](../fe-limit/) for $w$-fault boundedness.

Semantically the two sides are the same ZX-diagram; only the noise annotation changes. A *fault gadget* is a red spider connected by fault-free edges to its targets (here Z-spiders, whose phase-free Z-flips it describes) and by a noisy *spawning edge*, annotated with the weight of the fault, to a one-legged green spider. A flip on the spawning edge spreads to the targets, so the gadget models one atomic fault; without a flip it does nothing. As in the paper, noisy edges are labelled with their weight (the cost of a flip on that edge; a vector of weights for the $X$-, $Y$- and $Z$-flips, unlabelled noisy edges have weight 1), and *fault-free* (idealised) edges are drawn bold purple. These annotations are shown on the rule as stated; derived variants (transpose, colour swap, other legs counts) may drop them.
conditions: w ≥ w′ or w = − (fault-free); fault boundedness only, in one direction.
